questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Why is composition the natural test for inverse functions?
questions.prompt_markup: Why is composition the natural test for inverse functions?

choices.text: Composition adds the two functions, and inverses must add to 0 for every input x.
Composition reverses the graph across the x-axis, which is where an inverse must lie.
An inverse undoes the function, so applying one after the other must return the original input.
Two functions are inverses exactly when their product f(x) · g(x) is equal to 1 for every x.

questions.correct_answer: An inverse undoes the function, so applying one after the other must return the original input.
questions.grading_note: f(g(x)) = x and g(f(x)) = x. The others describe adding, reflecting over the x-axis, or multiplying, none of which is the inverse relationship.
